clue.text: Quick resolution — not quite what you bargained for?

definitions.text: not quite what you bargained for?

parts.note: quick means short, as in a short visit
a measure is a resolution or proposal put to a meeting or parliament

explanation.surface: A speedy settlement that leaves you feeling you did not get the deal you expected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quick resolution' reads as one idea, a fast settlement, but splits into two plain synonyms.
explanation.definitionFit: Being given less than the amount paid for, as a short pint, is literally not quite the bargain struck.

clue.text: Compatible notes written about clubs in terrace

indicators.note: written about tells us the notes are set down turned round, read backwards

parts.note: mi is a note of the sol-fa scale; two of them are mis

indicators.note: in places the clubs within the terrace word

parts.note: a patio is a paved terrace
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: Like-minded messages scribbled about a golf club on a patio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written about' turns the notes backwards; 'clubs' is the card suit, not golf clubs or nightclubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Simpatico, borrowed from Italian and Spanish, describes someone congenial and well suited to another person.

clue.text: Dilapidated house not left standing

indicators.note: a dilapidated building has fallen into disorder, so these letters are knocked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A tumbledown house that is no longer standing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left standing' looks like part of the house's description, but it is the definition: to leave someone standing is to beat them easily.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave rivals standing is to surpass them completely, which is exactly what excelling over others in brilliance means.

clue.text: Possibly keep barge horse?

definitions.meaning: a keep is the strongest ... of a castle, so a tall fortified building may be one
a horse on a towpath pulls (tows) a barge along a canal, making it one that tows

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the word as TOW plus the -ER of a doer, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A castle keep is a type of fortified tower, and a horse hauling a barge is literally something that tows.

clue.text: With king banished, émigré at length set forth

indicators.note: banished says the king's letter is sent out of the word for the émigré

parts.note: an émigré lives outside their native country, an expatriate
R, from Latin rex, is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: An exile, the king having been driven out, finally departed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at length' looks like 'eventually' in the surface, but with 'set forth' it means 'held forth in detail'.
explanation.definitionFit: To expatiate is to speak or write at great length about a subject, explaining it in detail.

clue.text: Two things dawn may bring for insectivore

parts.note: daybreak brings the rising sun and also morning moisture on the grass, dew
daybreak brings the rising sun and also morning moisture on the grass, dew

explanation.surface: A riddle about what daybreak delivers, ending oddly with an insect-eater.
explanation.definitionFit: The sundew is a carnivorous bog plant that traps insects on sticky glistening hairs and digests them.

clue.text: Prepare to fight again behind military leader

parts.note: behind as a noun means the rear

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Getting ready for battle once more, falling in behind the army commander.
explanation.definitionFit: To rearm is to supply weapons again, readying forces for renewed combat.

clue.text: Mess up part of drill, keeping quiet

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the drill part wraps around the word for quiet

parts.note: a bit is the cutting part fitted into a drill
a low voice is a quiet one

explanation.surface: Making a hash of a drill exercise while trying to stay silent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drill' suggests military practice; here it is the tool.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, to blow something is to bungle or waste a chance, so this phrase means botch it.

clue.text: Left in open country, one often gets drunk

indicators.note: in places the letter for left inside the open land word

parts.note: a heath is open, uncultivated land

explanation.surface: Someone left out in the wilds who regularly gets intoxicated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets drunk' suggests a person drinking; it is a toast that is drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A toast to someone's wellbeing ('Good health!') is drunk, often many times over an evening.

clue.text: Landed outside one mile boundary

indicators.note: outside means the landing word sits around the other letters

parts.note: lit is a past tense of light, to land or settle, as a bird alights
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Coming down just beyond a one-mile perimeter.
explanation.definitionFit: A limit is the boundary or furthest extent of an area.

clue.text: Writer cheers during solemn watch, causing division in north

indicators.note: during says these pieces come in the middle of the vigil word

parts.note: a wake is a vigil kept over a dead body
a pen is a writing instrument
ta is British slang for thanks, as is cheers

explanation.surface: An author toasting at a funeral vigil and causing a rift up north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'causing division' reads as a quarrel; it is an old administrative division. A wapentake was a subdivision of a county in northern and eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Wapentakes were historical subdivisions of shires such as Yorkshire, equivalent to the hundreds of southern England.

clue.text: Brave don penning article

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so the clothing verb surrounds the article

parts.note: to don clothes is to put them on, wear them
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A courageous university lecturer writing a piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'don' and 'penning' suggest an academic writing; 'don' is a verb, 'penning' is enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: To brave a storm or crisis is to come through it safely, a verb sense sharing a word with the climate.

clue.text: Current queen entering London street with large cast

indicators.note: cast means thrown away, so the letter for large is dropped
entering means going into, so the queen letters go inside the street name

parts.note: The Mall is the ceremonial avenue in London leading to Buckingham Palace
R, for Regina, abbreviates queen
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: The monarch processing down a London avenue with a big company of actors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' looks like a theatrical troupe but means discarded: R inside THE MALL gives THERMALL, minus one L.
explanation.definitionFit: A thermal is a rising current of warm air used by gliders and soaring birds.

clue.text: Like warning signs Alan Turing devised, changing number for radius

indicators.note: devised means made up or contrived, so the letters are reworked into a new order
changing one thing for another tells us one letter is swapped out for a different one

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for radius in geometry

explanation.surface: Road signs supposedly designed by the codebreaker Alan Turing, with a mathematical tweak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing number for radius' swaps one N in ALAN TURING for R; 'devised' then rearranges ALARTURING.
explanation.definitionFit: British road warning signs are three-cornered, red-bordered shapes, so their form is this geometric adjective.

clue.text: Brazen manoeuvres UN has made

indicators.note: manoeuvres are deliberate movements, so the letters are shifted into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A bold military exercise carried out by the United Nations.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone brazen behaves shamelessly, without any embarrassment or guilt.

clue.text: Wayside flower not very sharply cut

indicators.note: not says the letter for very is left out

parts.note: vetch is a climbing plant of the pea family common on verges

explanation.surface: A roadside bloom that has not been mown very closely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not very sharply cut' reads as one phrase about mowing; 'not very' is the deletion and 'sharply cut' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To etch is to cut a design into metal or glass with acid or a sharp point.

clue.text: Nameless local chasing temporary accommodation with no confidence

indicators.note: chasing means following behind, so the local word comes after the shelter word

parts.note: a tent is shelter put up for a short stay

indicators.note: nameless means losing N, the abbreviation for name, from the word for a local

parts.note: a local is a native of the place

explanation.surface: An anonymous resident following a campsite, lacking any self-assurance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'local' could be a pub in British usage; here it is a resident.
explanation.definitionFit: A tentative step is hesitant and uncertain, taken without assurance.

clue.text: Censured delegate was on the move

parts.note: a rep is a representative, a delegate
roved means wandered, travelled about

explanation.surface: A representative got reprimanded for travelling around.
explanation.definitionFit: Reproved means rebuked or criticised formally, a close synonym of censured.

clue.text: Apply oneself to doubles after change of ends

indicators.note: a change of ends, as in tennis, says the first and last letters trade places
after the swap the closing letter must sit at the front

parts.note: twos are doubles, pairs

explanation.surface: Playing doubles at tennis and switching ends between games.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change of ends' swaps the outer letters of TWOS; tennis players change ends during a match.
explanation.definitionFit: To swot is British slang for studying hard, applying oneself to books.

clue.text: Feast before cutting down

indicators.note: cutting means slicing into, so the prefix goes inside the word for unhappy

parts.note: down means unhappy, sad
pre is a prefix meaning before

explanation.surface: A banquet held before a bit of felling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down' is the adjective for gloomy, not a direction.
explanation.definitionFit: A spread is a large, lavish meal laid out on a table.

clue.text: Itinerant men and ladies devouring last of free cakes

indicators.note: devouring means taking inside, so the jumbled letters swallow another
itinerant means wandering, so these letters roam into a new order
last of picks the closing letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Travelling men and women gobbling up free pastries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devouring' puts E (last of 'free') into the shuffled MEN and LADIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Madeleines are small shell-shaped French sponge cakes, made famous by Proust.

clue.text: State capital's second terminus erected within a couple of years

indicators.note: within places the turned word inside the pair of year letters

parts.note: Y abbreviates year, so two years give two Ys

indicators.note: erected means set upright, which in a down clue turns the word upwards, backwards

parts.note: a terminus is an end

explanation.surface: A capital city's second railway terminus put up within two years.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'erected' means read upwards, so the end runs backwards; 'State' here is an Australian state.
explanation.definitionFit: Sydney is the capital of New South Wales, an Australian state.

clue.text: Setter's appearing in tolerable climbing gear from the East

indicators.note: in places the setter words inside the turned word for acceptable
climbing in a down clue means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: OK means acceptable, tolerable
the setter refers to themself: setter is = I am, shortened
appearing on stage is being on

explanation.surface: The puzzle's author turning up in passable mountaineering kit from Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing gear' reads as rope and crampons, but 'climbing' is the upward reversal in this down clue and 'gear' starts the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The kimono is the traditional Japanese robe, clothing from the Far East.

clue.text: What Cupid drew, heading off after artist and explorer

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: Cupid is one of Santa's reindeer, which pull a sleigh

explanation.surface: A painter puzzling over what the god of love sketched, then setting off as an adventurer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cupid' suggests the god of love, but is Santa's reindeer; 'drew' means pulled, not sketched.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Walter Raleigh was an Elizabethan adventurer who voyaged to the Americas.

clue.text: Cash primarily what's tempting fences?

indicators.note: fences means encloses, so the enticement word surrounds the letter

parts.note: a lure is an enticement, what tempts

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, taking the opening letter

explanation.surface: Is money what mainly lures receivers of stolen goods?
explanation.walkthrough: 'fences' suggests dealers in stolen goods; it means surrounds. The whole clue doubles as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucre is money, especially gained dishonourably, the very thing that tempts dealers in stolen goods.

clue.text: Dispatch impertinent player from team

definitions.meaning: to dispatch a letter onward is to send it on
an attacking player in football or rugby

explanation.definitionFit: The word means to send on mail, to be cheekily presumptuous, and an attacking position in team sports.

clue.text: Animal tucks in, if turning up truffles, say

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue reverses, reading the result upwards
tucks in means gets inside, so the beast goes into the two-letter word

parts.note: a gnu is a wildebeest

explanation.surface: A beast eats its fill, if it digs up truffles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucks in' looks like eating but means going inside; 'turning up' reverses the whole in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Truffles are underground mushrooms, an example of the kingdom including moulds and mushrooms.

clue.text: Those running last once regularly backed by Merry Monarch

indicators.note: merry suggests tipsy, so these letters are jumbled
backed means turned back, so the picked letters run in reverse
regularly picks every other letter

explanation.surface: Last runners regularly supported by Charles II, the Merry Monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Merry Monarch' is Charles II's nickname but here 'Merry' shuffles MONARCH; 'regularly' takes NE from 'once', 'backed' makes EN.
explanation.definitionFit: In a relay the anchor runs the final leg, so these runners are the closing members of teams.

clue.text: Oscar's dipping into sordid material

indicators.note: dipping into means going inside, so the letter enters the word for sordid

parts.note: vile means foul, sordid
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Oscar Wilde dabbling in something sleazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Voile is a thin, semi-transparent fabric of cotton or silk used for curtains and dresses.

clue.text: Little Mo's racket not the main attraction?

parts.note: a mo is a moment, and a little one is a second
a racket is a swindle, a fiddle

explanation.surface: Little Mo, the tennis champion Maureen Connolly, and her racket as a sideshow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little Mo' and 'racket' conjure tennis; they are a short time and a scam.
explanation.definitionFit: To play the subordinate role, like a second violinist, is not to be the star of the show.
